question: Can a stochastic positive control SPA — where action genuinely changes P(next_state | state) by mixing deterministic hash routing with uniform random candidate selection — validate KSG CMI and likelihood-ratio estimator sensitivity (positive_control_k3 >= 0.5 bits) while preserving |shuffled-action null_mean| < 0.1 bits at N=5000, thereby closing the C3 test-design gap that blocked the frozen verdict in EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440?
hypothesis: H0 (null): Neither KSG CMI nor likelihood-ratio achieves BOTH |shuffled-action null_mean| < 0.1 bits AND positive_control_k3 >= 0.5 bits on the stochastic SPA at N=5000. H1 (alternative): At least one of KSG CMI or likelihood-ratio achieves BOTH |null_mean| < 0.1 bits AND positive_control_k3 >= 0.5 bits on the stochastic SPA at N=5000. H2 (beyond-Markov, conditional on H1): K3 CMI - K2 CMI > 0.1 bits with bootstrap 95% CI lower > 0.0 at N=5000 on the stochastic SPA.
falsifier: C1 (null centering): For every estimator, |shuffled-action null_mean| >= 0.1 bits at N=5000. C3 (positive control sensitivity): For every estimator passing C1, positive_control_k3 < 0.5 bits. C6 (SPA design): Fewer than 48/48 (state, action) pairs with 4 distinct candidates. C7 (stratum coverage): Fewer than 2 non-empty stratum size buckets.

baselines.description: Weighted-averaged per-stratum Laplace-smoothed conditional PMI (parent null_mean=0.407 bits). Replicates parent bias floor.
KNN CMI estimator (k=5, alpha=1.0, parent null_mean=-0.262 bits).
baselines.expected: null_mean may shift sign or magnitude

baselines.description: KSG CMI on the parent's fully deterministic 8-state SPA. Expected CMI ~0 by construction for CMI estimators. Validates that the stochastic SPA produces non-zero CMI.

positive_control: Stochastic 12-state SPA: for each (state, action) transition, with probability 0.5 choose next state via deterministic hash routing (same as parent choose_next), and with probability 0.5 choose uniformly at random from CANDIDATES[state][action]. This creates I(Y;A|Z) > 0 by construction because P(Y|Z,A) != P(Y|Z) when action changes the deterministic-vs-stochastic mixture. Theoretical H(Y|Z,A) = 1.549 bits; theoretical I(Y;A|Z) depends on SPA structure but is expected to be 0.3-0.8 bits. Positive_control_k3 threshold: >= 0.5 bits (conservative, well above 0.1 null threshold). Permutation p <= 0.001.
null_control: Shuffled-action null: for each of 500 permutations, shuffle action labels within each session (preserving session structure and url_before/url_after pairing), recompute the estimator on the stochastic SPA, take the mean across permutations. The null mean must satisfy |mean| < 0.1 bits for any estimator to pass C1. Unit of permutation: action-label within session (same as parent).
measurement_validity: Stochastic SPA uses the same 12-state design, STATES, ACTIONS, and CANDIDATES as parent EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440.

SPA modification: choose_next_stochastic() replaces choose_next() — with probability 0.5 use hash routing, with probability 0.5 choose uniformly from CANDIDATES[current][action]. RNG seeded with seed=42 independently of session RNG.
Design verification: all 48/48 (state, action) pairs have 4 distinct candidates (inherited from parent CANDIDATES design, unchanged).
N=5000 transitions (50 sessions x 100 steps) with seed=42, same collection procedure as parent.
Strata with < 5 records are skipped (MIN_STRATUM_SIZE=5, same as parent).
KSG CMI implemented via sklearn.feature_selection.mutual_info_classif with k=5, alpha=1.0, discrete_features=True (same as parent).
Likelihood-ratio implemented via scipy.stats.chi2_contingency with Bonferroni correction (same as parent).
Bootstrap CI uses 200 trajectory-block resamples (same as parent).
Bonferroni correction for 5 primary comparisons (4 parent + 1 deterministic-SPA degenerate): alpha=0.01.
A separate deterministic SPA positive control (parent's 8-state SPA) is run to verify I(Y;A|Z)=0 for CMI estimators, confirming the stochastic SPA is needed.
If any estimator fails due to implementation issues, report as MEASUREMENT_INVALID with explicit error message.
decision_rule:
Verdict priority: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING > MEASUREMENT_INVALID > SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST.

FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING triggers if ANY of:
  (1) C1: All estimators have |shuffled-action null mean| >= 0.1 bits at N=5000
  (2) C3: For any estimator passing C1, positive_control_k3 < 0.5 bits OR permutation p > 0.001
  (3) C6: Fewer than 48/48 (state,action) pairs with 4 distinct candidates

MEASUREMENT_INVALID triggers if:
  (4) Fewer than 30% of (state,action) strata have >= 5 records at N=5000
  (5) stratum_size_bias_decomposition has < 2 non-empty size buckets
  (6) Any estimator implementation fails (e.g., missing dependency, convergence error)

SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of:
  (C1) At least 1 estimator has |null_mean| < 0.1 bits
  (C3) Positive control passes for that estimator (k3 >= 0.5 bits, p <= 0.001)
  (C6) Design check passes
  (C7) >= 2 non-empty size buckets

Phase 2 (beyond-Markov, only if SURVIVES on C1):
  (C2) K3 CMI - K2 CMI > 0.1 bits AND bootstrap 95% CI lower > 0.0
  (C4) |K2(N=50000) - K2(N=5000)| <= 0.3 bits for the best estimator

Note: C3 threshold is lowered from parent's 1.0 bit to 0.5 bits because:
- The parent's 1.0-bit threshold was calibrated for stratum PMI on deterministic SPA
- CMI estimators (KSG, LR) operate on a different scale
- Theoretical CMI on stochastic SPA is 0.3-0.8 bits depending on structure
- 0.5 bits is conservative (5x above null threshold) while being achievable
product_consequence_positive: If sensitivity validated (H1 passes): the C3 test-design gap is closed. KSG CMI and/or LR can detect genuine action-conditioned dynamics while maintaining null centering. The PMI research program is unblocked for beyond-Markov K3-K2 testing on the stochastic SPA. This opens the path to: (a) testing whether I(S_next; A | S_current, history) > 0 on this SPA class, (b) exploring KSG k-sensitivity and LR history-aware variants, (c) eventually testing on production SPAs with stochastic transitions.
product_consequence_negative: If sensitivity not validated (H0 confirmed): KSG CMI and LR cannot detect even a designed-in CMI signal of ~0.5 bits while maintaining null centering. The orthogonal-estimator pathway for Physics is closed for this SPA class. The Physics lane must pivot to: (a) fundamentally different detection paradigms (entropy rate, channel capacity, causal discovery), (b) production Web data with alternative state representations, or (c) abandoning synthetic SPA simulation entirely.
estimated_cost: Low-medium. Single Python script execution on stochastic 12-state SPA, N=5000 primary + N=50000 convergence test. ~15-20 minutes compute. 500 shuffled-action permutations. No browser/network required. Uses parent run_experiment.py infrastructure with modified choose_next_stochastic().
expected_information_gain: Very high. This experiment directly resolves the critical blocker from EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440: the C3 test-design gap. A definitive answer in either direction closes one pathway and opens the other. The experiment is small, clean, and resolves the highest-uncertainty question in the Physics lane's current state. If positive, it validates the estimator toolkit for all future CMI-based tests. If negative, it definitively closes the CMI pathway and forces a paradigm shift.
